title: Artificial Intelligence Beyond Glass
summary: Work through Artificial Intelligence Beyond Glass.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Artificial Intelligence Beyond Glass**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, The Causal Boundary, § Artificial Intelligence Beyond Glass
blocks.md: When an image classifier mislabels a warehouse photograph on a server, a downstream filter can discard the label before any machine moves; when a mobile robot's policy misjudges aisle clearance and drives its wheel motors, the chassis is already accelerating toward the rack. Across offline advisory prediction, digital agency, and physical embodiment, computation acquires different consequences as its outputs enter an action loop, and physical AI diverges from the other two in how agency, time, and recovery behave (a later section).

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Physical AI scope test matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A system is physical AI only when it has a learned statistical model, consequential physical feedback, and delegated authority at once; an independent deterministic veto does not remove delegated authority, while per-command human approval does.

questions.q: The section **Artificial Intelligence Beyond Glass** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: The running machine is specified once by a card of registry parameters, each tagged with its evidence category, which later chapters read rather than restate.

A learned model may only propose; an independent permission path with bounded latency, which the model cannot delay or corrupt, alone admits an action after checking fresh evidence, the stopping envelope, and a feasible fallback, and it acts on its own when the proposer stalls.

Work delivered across the causal boundary has no checkpoint to restore, so recovery is a new constrained motion limited by torque, friction, and drive limits, and the permission path must confirm that a feasible recovery still exists before it admits an action.

A system is physical AI only when it has a learned statistical model, consequential physical feedback, and delegated authority at once; an independent deterministic veto does not remove delegated authority, while per-command human approval does.
